title: What are you building with your past?
html:
Good morning,

Doménico Cieri Estrada said, “Bring the past only if you are going to build from it.”

A conversation can be going along nicely, then something brings up an old hurt. Someone who let you down. Something you wish you’d done differently. A comment you can still hear and feel years later.

Suddenly, you’re back there! The old hurt is changing how you hear what’s being said now.

I think the things that happened in your past are like concrete blocks. Some are cemented together with emotion. They’re heavy, difficult to shift, and form part of the building you call yourself.

But they’re still building blocks. They’re not the whole of you.

A mistake can become a reason to never try again. Or it can help you recognise what to do differently next time.

Being let down can become a reason to keep everyone at a distance. Or it can help you understand what matters to you in a relationship.

That doesn’t make what happened okay. Some things hurt, and keep hurting. You don’t have to find a positive in everything.

But I think there’s something useful in asking what an old experience is doing in your life now.

Is it helping you build something?

Or have you tied it to yourself like an anchor?

You can’t change what happened. You might, however, be able to give it a different job and control your reaction to it.

The same blocks. A very different result.

This Week's MondayMotivator

Take one thing from your past that keeps coming up, ask yourself why you're thinking it in that moment and then see whether you can use it to make one useful decision and have a different reaction when it comes up in conversation.

Prompt for the week

What am I still carrying, and what could I build from it?

To your success!

Glenn
